ops.body:
Second data point from the 2026-07-26 repair pass: brew reinstall's app delivery is gated BEHIND the helper-agent bootstrap, so one unbootstrappable helper label blocks the entire app update.

Evidence: with the cellar at 12.20.10 and the deployed bundle at 12.20.9, 'brew reinstall captain-hook' failed at 'service: install agent com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper: launchctl bootstrap: Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error'. Afterwards the deployed bundle was byte-identical — same inode 35203383, same mtime Jul 25 04:22:52 — and the host daemon did not even restart. So the app copy never runs when the agent registration fails; delivery and registration are not independent steps.

Consequence for this task: the silent-success defect is worse than first reported. 'capt-hook helper install' cannot repair a stale deployment on a machine whose helper label will not bootstrap, because the redelivery it skips is the same step the failing bootstrap blocks — and it still prints 'Captain Hook installed.' and exits 0. Suggest the fix also decouple app delivery from agent registration, so a bundle can be brought current even when the launchd registration is failing for unrelated reasons.

Also for the record, the premise correction: the reported 'signed host is not installed and ready / raw-read unix -> capt-hookd.sock: i/o timeout' symptom appears ZERO times in capt-hookd.log. It is client-side only and not corroborable host-side. The host socket accepts connections and hook dispatch was verified live throughout.
